science.qualification: Photosphere color from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum, dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 5,340 K and log g 4.55 (u1 0.563, u2 0.191): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The disc is unresolved: no map or absolute brightness is implied. Self-luminous, so no lighting.

science.label: Apr 2015
science.description: Radial component of the star's large-scale magnetic field, fitted with ZDIpy to 15 ESPaDOnS spectra of 25 March 2015 to 10 April 2015 (reduced chi-square 1.40, against 5.2 with no field); mean field 22 G. A reduction made in this project, not a published map. Black line: 67 degrees south, below which the star never faces us.
science.title: ESPaDOnS · magnetic map made here · Apr 2015

science.label: Sector 22
science.description: Brightness of the star's surface that reproduces its light as it turns once in 9.04 days, fitted with starry to the TESS mission's own 2-minute light curve of sector 22 (its PDC-MAP flux) (the light varies by 0.83%; the map's curve leaves a scatter of 0.15%, the light's own noise being 0.03%). A light curve fixes how bright each longitude is, not the latitude of what darkens it. In this sector the method of Holcomb et al. (2022, ApJ 936, 138) finds a period of 10.94 d from the autocorrelation, whose peaks have a height of 0.18, a width of 0.50 and a fit of 0.99, and in all 2 of the star's sectors together a period of 4.52 d from the autocorrelation, whose peaks have a height of 0.19, a width of 0.45 and a fit of 0.96; its criteria accept that as the star's rotation. The light repeats every 4.52 days, half the rotation period the catalogues print for the star: two groups of spots on opposite sides do that. The map is made at the tilt the page draws the star with, 67°. Gaia DR3 lists 1 other star within 63 arcseconds, with under 0.1% of their light and the star's together. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · brightness map made here · Sector 22

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#ffeadf, its Color dataset) over the brightness map this project made from the star's light in TESS sector 22 (February and March 2020): the map's scale, 97.5% to 102.5% of the mean surface, runs from a darker, richer tone of the same hue to the color itself. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the parts can be told apart: the darkest part gives 3.9% less light than the brightest. Longitudes are fixed by the light curve; latitudes and shapes are not. No color change of the spots is drawn: none is measured. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · the star in its color over its brightness map · February and March 2020
